commands.description: What every agent must never run on a box (ADR 0043): any other command runs, because the walls are outside the agent (its own Linux user, read-only keys, every process killed at the end, the box's own push). Each agent's adapter writes this as its own rules, for every part of a command and after git's own options too (git -C x push). The box pushes, so an agent never pushes or stashes. web: it may read the web with its own tools.

openrouter.description: OpenRouter: hundreds of models through one key, some free (models ending :free; 50 requests a day, 1,000 with $10 of credits bought once)

claude.description: Claude Code, headless (ADR 0031): it only thinks. On a box it runs as the slot's own Linux user, in its own clone, with read-only keys; it edits and commits there, reads the web and the tools' look calls, and writes result.json. It never pushes (apply does) and never stashes. Tasks send the prompt on stdin; its adapter adds the model, the effort, the commands every agent must never run, the look tools and its output format. models, efforts and modelPattern say what a `use` line may pick; auto is the default.

about.sonnet: Most work: changes, questions, daily jobs
about.fable: The most capable; the heaviest on your plan

pi.description: pi, headless (ADR 0038): a small agent core that does the work its own way, held to the same rules as every agent by Shipify's gate. Its models come through a gateway (OpenRouter here), by their ids there: the few below listed first (the free ones first, then cheap ones paid from the gateway's credits), or any other the gateway has (/models <word> and the web chat's chip find them). Its key is the gateway's.
